title: Candidi Ariani Epistola ad Marium Victorinum Rethorem
author: Marius Victorinus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp114.tmp114.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Arii ad Eusebium : « Domino desideratissimo, ho- mini Dei fideli, recta opinanti. Artus qui persecu- tionem patitur ab Alexandro papa injuste, propter omnia vincentem veritatem, pro qua et tu propug- nas, in Domino salvum esse.
passages.english: [Letter] of Arius to Eusebius: "To [my] most longed-for lord, a faithful man of God, of right opinion: Arius, who suffers persecution unjustly from Pope Alexander on account of the all-conquering truth, for which you too contend, [wishes you] to be well in the Lord.
passages.notes: 'Artus' is a scanning error for 'Arius'; 'ho- mini', 'persecu- tionem' and 'propug- nas' are words split across lines. 'Papa' here is the title of Alexander, bishop of Alexandria, and is rendered 'Pope'. The Latin 'Domino desideratissimo' may also be read 'to [my] most beloved lord'.

passages.original: Sic autem diximus, juxta quod nec pars Dei est; nec ex subjecto aliquo : idcirco persequimur. Jam tu scis. Confortari te in Domino, preces facio, memorem tribulationum nostrarum, Collucianista, vere Ευσέ- βιε. » Haec Arius dicit.
passages.english: And we have spoken thus, to the effect that he is neither a part of God nor from any substrate; for this reason we are persecuted. You already know the rest. I pray that you be strengthened in the Lord, mindful of our tribulations, fellow-Lucianist, truly Eusebius." This is what Arius says.
passages.notes: This is the close of Arius' letter to Eusebius of Nicomedia, quoted in Latin. "Collucianista" means fellow-pupil of Lucian (of Antioch). "Ευσέ- βιε" is the Greek vocative Eusebie, split by the scan. It puns on the name: "truly Eusebius" means "truly pious." "Jam tu scis" is rendered loosely as "You already know the rest"; literally it is "Now you know."
